label.en: Asks you to share an OTP / PIN / CVV / password

why.en: No bank, government office or genuine company needs your OTP, PIN or CVV. Sharing it hands over your money.

examples: Please share the OTP you just received to confirm.
Kindly send your CVV to verify the card.
counterExamples: Never share your OTP with anyone.
We will never ask you to share your OTP or PIN.

label.en: Asks you to install a remote-access / screen-share app

why.en: Screen-sharing apps let the caller watch your screen and your OTPs and operate your banking apps.

examples: Install AnyDesk so our officer can help you.
Please start screen sharing now.

label.en: Pushes an APK / unofficial app install

why.en: Apps installed from links (.apk) can read your SMS and OTPs. Genuine providers use the official Play Store/App Store.

examples: Download this apk from the link.
Install the app from http://x.top/bill.apk
counterExamples: Get our app on the Play Store.

label.en: 'Digital arrest' / safe-account / arrest-warrant language

why.en: There is no 'digital arrest' in Indian law. Fake officers use it to scare victims into paying.

examples: You are under digital arrest.
Transfer the amount to the RBI safe account.

label.en: Tells you to stay on the call / not tell anyone

why.en: Isolating the victim ('don't tell your family', 'stay on video') is a core part of the scam script.

examples: Do not disconnect the video call.
Don't tell anyone about this, including family.
counterExamples: Please call us back when free.

label.en: Parcel / courier linked to drugs or illegal items

why.en: A 'seized parcel in your name' is the standard opening of the fake-police scam.

examples: A parcel in your name was seized with drugs.
Illegal items were found in your courier.
counterExamples: Your parcel is out for delivery.
The courier will arrive by 5 pm.

label.en: Claims to be police / CBI / customs / a regulator

why.en: Impersonating authority creates fear so you stop thinking. Verify by calling the office on its official number.

examples: This is the CBI calling about your case.
Inspector Verma from Cyber Crime Branch.
counterExamples: Happy birthday from all of us.

label.en: Artificial urgency / deadline

why.en: Scammers rush you so you don't verify. Real institutions give written notice and time.

examples: Pay within 2 hours or lose access.
Final notice, act now.
counterExamples: Your order will arrive next week.

label.en: Threatens to block / suspend your account, SIM or service

why.en: Threats of blocking are used to force a quick click or call. Check the status in the official app instead.

examples: Your account will be blocked today.
Your SIM card will be deactivated.

label.en: KYC / PAN update demand

why.en: Banks do not ask you to update KYC through links or by sharing OTPs over SMS/WhatsApp.

examples: Your KYC update is pending.
Update your PAN immediately.

label.en: Electricity-bill disconnection threat

why.en: 'Your power will be cut tonight' with a number to call is a widespread scam that often ends in an APK install.

examples: Your electricity bill is unpaid and supply disconnect tonight.
Your power supply will be cut tonight.
counterExamples: Your order is on the way.

label.en: Guaranteed / unrealistic investment returns

why.en: Guaranteed or very high returns do not exist in legitimate investing.

examples: Guaranteed returns of 30% per day.
Double your money in a week.
counterExamples: Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks.

label.en: VIP stock group / IPO-allotment / trading-tip lure

why.en: Invite-only groups with 'expert' tips are how investment scams recruit victims.

examples: Join our VIP group for stock tips.
You are added to the exclusive channel.

label.en: Part-time job / 'task' earning scheme

why.en: Paid-per-task jobs that later ask for deposits are a known scam pattern.

examples: Part-time job: like videos and earn money.
Work from home and earn Rs 5000 per day.
counterExamples: We have a full-time opening in Pune.

label.en: Asks you to pay a fee/deposit to receive money or unlock earnings

why.en: Genuine prizes, loans, jobs and refunds do not require you to pay first.

examples: Pay a registration fee to withdraw your earnings.
A refundable deposit is needed to release funds.

label.en: Prize / lottery you never entered

why.en: You cannot win a lottery you did not enter. Fees to 'claim' prizes are the scam.

examples: You have won a lottery of 25 lakh.
Claim your prize today.
counterExamples: The lottery results are on the news.

label.en: Instant-loan / loan-app lure

why.en: Predatory loan apps harvest contacts and photos and are linked to harassment.

examples: Instant loan approved without documents.
Pre-approved loan for you.
counterExamples: Your home loan EMI is due.

label.en: Refund / 'sent by mistake' pretext

why.en: Refund pretexts are used to get you to approve a payment request or share credentials.

examples: Your refund is pending, click here.
The money was wrongly transferred to you.

label.en: Asks you to scan a QR / enter UPI PIN to RECEIVE money

why.en: You never need a PIN or QR scan to receive money. If a PIN is requested, money is leaving your account.

examples: Scan this QR to receive the refund.
Enter your UPI PIN to receive money.
counterExamples: Scan the QR to pay at the shop.

label.en: 'Hi Mum/Dad, new number' or emergency money request

why.en: Impersonating a relative from a 'new number' is a common WhatsApp scam.

examples: Hi mum, I lost my phone, this is my new number.
Emergency at hospital, send money now.
